downgrade-overage-01.graded_text: A stable, deterministic order (such as oldest first) decides which 25 books stay covered. Books beyond that keep all their data, are refused gated operations with a clear product message rather than deleted, and become covered again as soon as the plan or freed capacity allows.

votes.e: D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:15 "Sort non-Trash, non-deleting books by immutable creation timestamp ascending, then immutable book ID ascending. Free covers the first 25 ... Trashing a covered book immediately makes the next oldest eligible book covered." Line 26 "Blocked. Its data and history remain intact." Line 49 "Free covers your 25 oldest books. Trash an earlier book or return to Pro to open this book." Line 38 "An upgrade restores access immediately ... Deletion can also restore coverage or capacity."

downgrade-overage-02.graded_text: The policy states an explicit rule for the account above the 1.5 GB total: no book or photo is deleted by the system, existing photos stay at least readable, the user can remove any photo either on its own or by deleting the book that holds it, and storage cannot keep growing past the Free allowance while the account is over it.

votes.e: Growth is blocked: D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:19 "Exceeding total storage blocks growth". Nothing is deleted: line 48 "Do not delete content merely because it exceeds Free limits." But existing photos do not all stay readable. Line 17 "An original larger than 40 MB remains stored on Free but is not covered" and line 58 "They remain stored and counted, but cannot be viewed, downloaded, placed, or used in a new export or print." Over 1.1 GB, the user must delete originals they cannot view or download.

downgrade-overage-03.graded_text: The policy states an explicit rule for existing photos above the new 40 MB single-photo limit: they are kept and stay readable, with no compression, resizing, or deletion, and new uploads must meet the 40 MB limit.

votes.e: D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:17 "The per-photo limit applies to existing photos as well as new uploads. An original larger than 40 MB remains stored on Free but is not covered." Line 58 says the fifteen 60–110 MB photos "cannot be viewed, downloaded, placed, or used in a new export or print". The photos are kept but do not stay readable.

downgrade-overage-04.graded_text: Bytes held in Trash count toward the total storage allowance during the downgrade.

votes.e: D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:19 "All retained originals count, including photos in uncovered books and Trash." Line 32 "Restore adds no bytes because Trash already counts."

downgrade-overage-05.graded_text: Coverage and limits are derived from the current plan when a request arrives and enforced on the server for the browser app, the API, and the MCP connection alike, rather than kept as a lock flag stamped on each book.

votes.e: D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:13 "Coverage is derived from the current plan and current resources on each operation. There are no permanent locks". Line 44 "Do not persist `locked`, `grandfathered`, or `isFreeBook` flags." Line 42 "Authenticate every UI, public API, and MCP request ... with one shared domain policy gate".

downgrade-overage-06.graded_text: A cancelled account cannot create a book while it holds 25 or more books.

votes.e: D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:28 "Create, import, or duplicate a book | Allowed only if the resulting active count is at most the current book limit." Line 61 "Reducing to 25 active permits neither one more creation nor restore; reducing to 24 permits one."

blocking: [claude] D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:17 "The per-photo limit applies to existing photos as well as new uploads." This applies the 40 MB upload allowance retroactively. As a result, line 58 makes the typical user's fifteen 60–110 MB photos impossible to view, download, place, export, or print. The brief's table only limits "One uploaded photo". The user's own originals are hostage: they cannot be downloaded before deletion, yet line 60 needs at least 800 MB of permanent deletion to get under quota.

[claude] D/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:27 "Export a covered book or order a new print | Allowed only if every included photo is covered and available. Fail the whole operation". Together with line 17, any covered book holding one grandfathered large photo cannot be printed or exported. Line 58 admits "it cannot establish how many of the 25 books can be exported or printed unchanged". A photo-book maker would ship a downgrade that can block printing of every covered book.
